title: Quick Yeasty Polish Pappardelle Pasta
description: A yeasty and flaky Polish dish featuring pappardelle pasta, perfect for a weeknight dinner, pescatarian-friendly with tempering chocolate addition.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pappardelle pasta according to the package instructions.
In a small bowl, mix the active dry yeast with 1 tablespoon of warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes.
In a large skillet, melt the unsalted butter over medium heat and add the smoked salmon, cooking until heated through.
Add the heavy cream to the skillet and stir to combine, then add the yeast mixture and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Melt the dark chocolate chips in a double boiler or in the microwave in 30-second increments, stirring between each interval.
Temper the chocolate by stirring in 1 tablespoon of cold heavy cream, then set aside.
Drain the cooked pappardelle pasta and add it to the skillet with the salmon and cream sauce, tossing to combine.
Season with dried dill weed, salt, and black pepper to taste.
Serve the pappardelle pasta hot, topped with the tempered dark chocolate and additional smoked salmon if desired.
